Manchester "Guardian" And
Drugs In North China

Publishes Story Of Miss Muriel Lester's Findings
With Editorial On Japanese Responsibility.
Alleged Big Number Of Drug Shops

LONDON, June 17.—The recent discoveries of Miss Muriel Lester, relative to the appalling conditions of drug traffic being carried on in the Demilitarized Zone in North China, were exposed in the Manchester "Guardian" this morning. The paper comes out to-day with an article on the subject from its special correspondent in Peiping and an editorial which deals with the Japanese responsibility for the situation.

Miss Lester, the founder of Kingsley Hall in the Bow district of London and a well-known English social reformer, spent nearly a month in North China recently, during which time she inspected the demilitarized area at the special request of certain authorities in Japan. The findings of her visit which are reported by her through the "Guardian's" correspondent, are of a sensational nature.

"Grave Responsibility"

The "grave responsibility of Japan" is stressed by the Manchester "Guardian's" editorial to-day. "The responsibility of Japan for the truly terrifying progress that has been made in accustoming the Chinese inhabitants of the area to the use of drugs is extremely grave, for there is good reason to believe that the essential drugs being provided the Chinese were not only allowed to slip through the territory controlled by Japan but that they have actually been distributed in the North with the connivance of the Japanese authorities," it writes.

"No impartial observer of the situation can refrain from the query whether the Japanese army, with all its ambitions concerning the territory to the South of the Great Wall, is not responsible for deliberately encouraging a traffic demoralising to Chinese citizens and one which will leave them incapable of resisting the moves at territorial expansion on the part of the Japanese."

The figures given in the information from Peiping reveal the existence of a great number of shops where drugs are sold to the local citizenry by Japanese and Korean dealers, who profit by the system of extraterritoriality in resisting the attempts of local authorities to suppress their trade.

Specific Complaints

In Changli, according to this article, there are 116 Japanese dealers and 47 Koreans, of which number 65 have set themselves up in the business since the beginning of the year. In the town of Liaoting, Miss Lester found a population of 30,000 catered to by no less than 200 drug establishments, both Japanese and Korean. The Tongshan and Kuyeh districts appear to suffer particularly keenly from the nefarious operations of the merchants. In Tongshan alone, it is learned that 500 to 550 drug-selling apothecary shops are at work among the miners.

The finder of this information is at present in Japan. Miss Lester was in Shanghai a week ago, arriving directly from Peiping.—Havas.

曼彻斯特《卫报》与
华北毒品问题

刊登穆里尔·莱斯特小姐调查结果的报道
并发表关于日本责任的社论。
据称存在大量毒品店铺

伦敦，6月17日电。——曼彻斯特《卫报》今晨披露了穆里尔·莱斯特小姐近期关于华北非军事区内令人震惊的毒品交易状况的发现。该报今日刊登了其驻北平特约记者就此主题撰写的文章，以及一篇论述日本对此局势负有责任的社论。

莱斯特小姐是伦敦鲍区金斯利大厅 (Kingsley Hall) 的创始人，也是英国著名的社会改革家。她最近应日本某些当局的特别请求，在华北度过了近一个月时间，期间视察了非军事区。她通过《卫报》记者报道的此次访问调查结果，性质轰动。

“重大责任”

曼彻斯特《卫报》今日的社论强调了“日本的重大责任”。社论写道：“日本对于该地区中国居民逐渐习惯使用毒品这一真正可怕的进展所负的责任极其重大，因为有充分理由相信，提供给中国人的主要毒品不仅被允许溜过日本控制的领土，而且实际上是在日本当局的默许下在北方进行分销的。”

“任何对该局势持公正态度的观察家都不得不提出这样的疑问：日本军队怀着对长城以南领土的所有野心，是否应对故意鼓励一种使中国公民道德沦丧、并使其无力抵抗日本领土扩张举动的交易负责。”

来自北平的信息中提供的数据揭示，存在大量由日本和朝鲜商人向当地市民出售毒品的店铺，这些商人利用治外法权体系来抵制地方当局镇压其贸易的尝试。

具体指控

根据这篇文章，在昌黎，有116名日本商人和47名朝鲜商人，其中65人是今年年初开始从事这一行业的。在滦县 (Liaoting) 镇，莱斯特小姐发现，拥有3万人口的小镇竟有多达200家毒品场所为其提供服务，这些场所既有日本人经营的，也有朝鲜人经营的。唐山和开滦地区似乎深受这些商人邪恶活动的危害。据悉，仅在唐山一地，就有500至550家贩卖毒品的药店在矿工中活动。

这些信息的发现者目前在日本。莱斯特小姐一周前曾在上海，她是直接从北平抵达的。——哈瓦斯通讯社。

THE DEMILITARIZED ZONE IN
GRIP OF DRUGS
Japanese and Koreans Worst Traffickers, Declares
Investigator: Extrality's Shelter

SHOCKED BY SHANGHAI FACTORY HOURS

Miss Muriel Lester, an internationally famous social worker, and the founder of Kingsley Hall in London, will leave Shanghai to-morrow for Tokyo, to tell the Japanese Government what she has discovered concerning the drug traffic conditions in North China's demilitarized zone. Miss Lester, who declares that she made the survey at the special request of a group of public-spirited Japanese and that she found the drug traffic in the North even worse than she had supposed possible, will sail on the ss. President Taft and will be gone for only one week.

In an interview with a representative of the "North-China Daily News," this noted social worker revealed that she found in Changli, a city of 15,000 inhabitants, and the centre of her investigations, more than 30 poisonous drug shops clustered outside the city wall, all belonging to Japanese or Koreans who claim extraterritorial rights which render them untouchable by Chinese officials. Certain especially unpleasant features which impressed her were the alliance of gambling, lotteries, brothels, and pawnshops with the drug traffic. She said:—

"When people bring their articles to the pawnshop, it is often suggested to them that they take heroin or morphine instead of money. If an injection is desired, a syringe is rented to the customer on the deferred payment system. The first dose is obtainable at a low price, but it rises swiftly as the customer becomes an addict. Lotteries are something quite new in the people's experience and the decrease in prosperity which has occurred during the last two years is due in great measure to the Japanese evading payment of the Customs duty on imported goods. One can purchase drugs for five cents and young people are freely served."

Women Ignored

Although the city was forced to open a clinic for drug addicts, there is no accommodation for women, Miss Lester stated. She also mentioned that, although 180 drug-shops have been set up in the county of Changli during the past two or three years, and 65 of them this year alone, the conditions in Changli are better than in some of the other cities of the demilitarized zone. The worst places she lists as Tangshan, Shanhaikuan, Lanhsien, Kaping, Kuyeh and Chinwangtao. The danger to young life in the community is so great that the inhabitants are setting up associations for good citizenship and are appealing to the public to guard against these evils.

Miss Lester denied that she was an "opium expert". She said:—"I have seen horrid sights in India and Hongkong, as well as in the demilitarized zone. I do not blame the Japanese for this, and I do not believe, as some do, that it is part of a secret Japanese foreign policy to sap the moral of the Chinese. Because the Japanese themselves are anxious to stamp out this evil, I have made this special survey."

Good and Bad in Shanghai

During her stay in Shanghai, Miss Lester, who has been engaged in social service work for 31 years, visited the Rickshaw Shelter, and several local factories. She was favourably impressed with the Shelter, which she described as "far in advance of similar institution I have yet seen." In direct contrast to the shelter, she admitted being "shocked and appalled" by factory conditions. "Too unbelievable for words," she said, was the fact that 12-hour shifts are worked by children, many of whom are between the ages of 8 and 9 years.

Miss Lester declared that she hardly could believe it possible that people were permitted to work as long as 16 hours at the changing of the shifts. She thinks that if all women in China would work together, these terrible factory conditions could be ameliorated.

"I ask you, British, American, and other foreign women, as well as the Chinese, to go through just one factory, and then I am sure you will do something about changing the conditions," she said.

Miss Lester will return to China this month and remain here until December, when she intends to sail for India, to attend the Indian Women's National Conference.

毒品掌控之中
调查员宣称日本人和朝鲜人是最大的贩毒者：受治外法权庇护

对上海工厂工时感到震惊

国际知名的社会工作者、伦敦金斯利大厅创始人穆里尔·莱斯特小姐将于明日离开上海前往东京，向日本政府通报她在华北非军事区发现的毒品交易状况。莱斯特小姐声称，她是应一群具有公共精神的日本人的特别请求进行此次调查的，并且发现北方的毒品交易情况比她预想的还要糟糕。她将乘坐“塔夫脱总统号”轮船 (ss. President Taft) 启程，行程仅为一周。

在接受《字林西报》代表采访时，这位著名的社会工作者透露，她在拥有1.5万人口的城市昌黎（也是她调查的中心）发现，城墙外聚集着30多家有毒毒品店铺，所有这些店铺都属于日本人或朝鲜人，他们声称拥有治外法权，使得中国官员无法触及他们。令她印象深刻的某些特别令人不快的特征是，赌博、彩票、妓院和当铺与毒品交易相互勾结。她说：—

“当人们把物品送到当铺时，经常有人建议他们领取海洛因或吗啡而不是现金。如果需要注射，会以分期付款的方式向顾客出租注射器。第一剂可以低价获得，但随着顾客成为瘾君子，价格迅速上涨。彩票在人们的经验中是完全新鲜的事物，而过去两年出现的繁荣衰退，在很大程度上是由于日本人逃避进口货物的关税所致。人们只需花五分钱就能买到毒品，年轻人可以随意购买。”

忽视女性

莱斯特小姐指出，虽然该市被迫开设了一家针对吸毒者的诊所，但没有为女性提供住宿。她还提到，虽然在过去的两三年里，昌黎县设立了180家毒品店，仅今年就有65家，但昌黎的情况比非军事区的其他一些城市要好。她列出的最糟糕的地方是唐山、山海关、滦县、开平、开滦和秦皇岛。社区中年轻生命面临的危险如此之大，以至于居民们正在建立良好公民协会，并呼吁公众防范这些罪恶。

莱斯特小姐否认自己是“鸦片专家”。她说：—“我在印度、香港以及非军事区都见过可怕的景象。我并不因此责怪日本人，我也不像有些人那样相信，这是日本秘密外交政策的一部分，旨在削弱中国人的道德。正因为日本人自己也急于根除这一罪恶，我才进行了这次特别调查。”

上海的好与坏

在上海逗留期间，从事社会服务工作31年的莱斯特小姐参观了人力车夫收容所和几家当地工厂。她对收容所印象深刻，形容其“远远优于我迄今见过的类似机构”。与收容所形成鲜明对比的是，她承认对工厂状况感到“震惊和惊恐”。她说，儿童实行12小时轮班制，其中许多孩子年龄在8到9岁之间，这一事实“难以置信，难以言表”。

莱斯特小姐表示，她几乎不敢相信人们被允许在换班时工作长达16小时。她认为，如果全中国的女性联合起来，这些可怕的工厂状况是可以改善的。

“我请求你们，英国、美国和其他外国女性，以及中国女性，去参观哪怕一家工厂，然后我相信你们一定会采取行动改变这种状况，”她说。

莱斯特小姐将于本月返回中国，并在此停留至12月，届时她打算乘船前往印度，参加印度妇女全国会议。

制作人：D. S. Umemoto。转呈人：O. J. Sverest

根据当地日本领事当局从东京警方收到的报告，穆里尔·莱斯特小姐在东京逗留期间的行踪如下：

10月19日 穆里尔·莱斯特小姐乘坐“浅间丸”号轮船（s.s. "Asama Maru"）从旧金山抵达横滨。

10月20日 下午，她向东京帝国大学的学生发表了题为“社会工作的精神”的演讲。
晚上，她在东京芝区的友会教堂（Friend (?) Church）讲述了她的工作。

Address by Miss Muriel Lester.

An address entitled "Voluntary Poverty" was delivered
by Miss Muriel Lester in the Community Church, Avenue Petain,
on December 27. Miss Lester described herself as a Christian
Socialist, and explained that she is guided by the laws of
Heaven as against the laws of the land as riches should be
distributed equitably. She and a band of helpers, convinced
that the economic and social problems of the world could be
solved by Christian socialism, founded a number of years ago
a movement known as the "Voluntary Poverty Group". She
quoted numerous texts from the scriptures in support of this
contention and added that the "Voluntary Poverty Group"
functions chiefly in the slum districts of the East End of
London and is able to relieve much suffering there by practising
self-denial among themselves. The individuals in the Group
retain sufficient of their income to provide them with the
daily needs of life, which are cut down to the barest minimum,
and the surplus reverts to the rightful owners - the poor.
She has disposed of a substantial legacy in this way herself.

During Miss Lester's travels in India, she found Mahatma
Gandhi to be an ideal Christian Socialist: one who has lived
his life with, and can speak for, the non-vocal masses; one
who can interpret their thoughts, their wants and their
ideals; one who can tell the nabobs and others that they have
no right to the riches they own. Gandhi is a "dear friend"
of Miss Lester's, and he allowed her the honour to be hostess
to him for a period of three months during his visit to England.

The speaker related numerous anecdotes concerning her
work among the poor and spoke with emphasis on the sacrifices
she had made on their behalf.

穆里尔·莱斯特小姐的演讲。

穆里尔·莱斯特小姐于12月27日在贝当路社区教堂发表了题为“自愿贫困”的演讲。莱斯特小姐自称是一名基督教社会主义者，并解释说，在财富应当公平分配的问题上，她遵循的是天律而非地法。她和一群助手深信世界的经济和社会问题可以通过基督教社会主义来解决，因此在数年前发起了一场名为“自愿贫困小组”的运动。她引用了大量圣经经文来支持这一观点，并补充说，“自愿贫困小组”主要在伦敦东区的贫民窟地区开展活动，通过成员间的自我克制，能够缓解那里的许多痛苦。小组成员保留足够的收入以维持每日的生活必需，这些必需品被削减到最低限度，而剩余部分则归还给真正的主人——穷人。她本人也以这种方式处置了一笔可观的遗产。

在莱斯特小姐游历印度期间，她发现圣雄甘地是一位理想的基督教社会主义者：一个与无声的大众生活在一起并能为他们代言的人；一个能诠释他们的思想、需求和理想的人；一个能告诉富豪和其他人，他们无权拥有其所占有的财富的人。甘地是莱斯特小姐的“挚友”，在他访问英国期间，他允许她荣幸地在三个月内担任他的女主人。

演讲者讲述了许多关于她在穷人中间工作的轶事，并着重强调了她为他们所做出的牺牲。

Questions were invited at the conclusion of the
address, and a lady sardonically asked whether it was
not a waste of money to furnish passages for globe-
trotters, much to the embarrassment of the speaker.
Other questions elicited the fact that only three small
Voluntary Poverty Groups, known by different names,
exist in England, a few in India, but none elsewhere,
although the speaker believed that Groups could be
founded in China.

The sarcasm and witticism volunteered during the
questioning period must have left the speaker with an
impression that her address was not convincing to the
audience of about 100.

Miss Lester announced in the course of the address
that she intends to visit India soon.

演讲结束时邀请提问，一位女士讽刺地问道，为环球旅行者提供旅费难道不是浪费金钱吗？这使演讲者颇为尴尬。其他问题揭示出这样一个事实：在英国只有三个小型的“自愿贫困小组”，名称各异，在印度有几个，但在其他地方则没有，尽管演讲者相信可以在中国建立此类小组。

提问期间出现的讽刺和俏皮话，必然给演讲者留下这样的印象：她的演讲未能说服在场约100名听众。

莱斯特小姐在演讲过程中宣布，她打算不久后访问印度。

KINGSLEY HALL
FOUNDER

Miss Muriel Lester Paying
Visit to Shanghai

Miss Muriel Lester, a distinguished English social worker, is to visit Shanghai next week. She is noted as one of the original promoters of the Fellowship of Reconciliation, but is even better known as the founder of Kingsley Hall, a settlement house in the East End of London.

Thirty-one years ago she got the vision of service and gave her life to the poor of London's slums. She and her sister started Kingsley Hall, a Christian social centre founded on voluntary poverty, put all their money into it and they have lived there ever since. Seven years ago Miss Lester went to India, spending a month with Tagore and another with Gandhi. Two years ago when Mr. Gandhi was in London for the Round-Table Conference he spent his entire three months with them at Kingsley Hall among the poor. Kingsley Hall is a centre of fellowship in the midst of a large industrial neighborhood, run for the most part by the people themselves. There is no paid labour at Kingsley Hall. This East End social work includes among its friends such men and women as Lord Lytton, Mrs. Sybil Thorndike, Mr. John Masefield, Sir Charles Trevelyan, Lady Astor, Viscount Knebworth, Mr. George Lansbury, and many others like Mr. A. A. Milne who showed his practical interest in donating a roof garden. The work has been so successful that a second Kingsley Hall was asked for and built in Dagenham, whilst a special building for children's work—the Children's House—is an active unit of the work in Bow.

Miss Lester was speaking in the United States during the summer; there, she was termed by one writer the "Jane Addams of England". During the latter part of November, and in December she has been speaking in North and Central China and is now in Nanking. She has spoken with great favour before large audiences, and it is hoped that Shanghai can give her an equally warm welcome during the busy holiday season. Miss Lester's first public speech will be delivered in Community Church on Wednesday, December 27, at 8.15 p.m.

穆里尔·莱斯特小姐访问上海

穆里尔·莱斯特小姐，一位杰出的英国社会工作者，将于下周访问上海。她以和解联谊会（Fellowship of Reconciliation）的早期发起人之一而闻名，但更为人所知的是她是伦敦东区金斯利大厅（Kingsley Hall，一处定居救助站）的创始人。

三十一年前，她产生了服务的愿景，并将自己的生命奉献给了伦敦贫民窟的穷人。她和她的姐姐创办了金斯利大厅，这是一个建立在自愿贫困基础上的基督教社会中心，她们将所有资金投入其中，并一直居住在那里。七年前，莱斯特小姐前往印度，与泰戈尔共度一个月，又与甘地共度一个月。两年前，当甘地先生在伦敦参加圆桌会议时，他在金斯利大厅的穷人中与他们共同度过了整整三个月。金斯利大厅是一个位于大型工业区中心的团契中心，主要由民众自己运营。金斯利大厅没有受薪劳工。这项东区社会工作拥有的朋友包括利顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）、西比尔·索恩代克夫人（Mrs. Sybil Thorndike）、约翰·梅斯菲尔德先生（Mr. John Masefield）、查尔斯·特里维廉爵士（Sir Charles Trevelyan）、阿斯特夫人（Lady Astor）、克内布沃斯子爵（Viscount Knebworth）、乔治·兰斯伯里先生（Mr. George Lansbury），以及许多其他人，如A. A. 米尔恩先生（Mr. A. A. Milne），他通过捐赠屋顶花园表示了实际的兴趣。这项工作非常成功，以至于有人要求并建造了第二个金斯利大厅，位于达格纳姆（Dagenham），而一座用于儿童工作的特殊建筑——儿童之家（Children's House）——是鲍（Bow）地区工作的一个活跃单元。

莱斯特小姐夏季在美国演讲；在那里，她被一位作家称为“英国的简·亚当斯”。11月下旬及12月，她在中国华北和华中进行演讲，目前身在南京。她在大型听众面前发表了备受好评的演讲，希望上海能在繁忙的节日季节给予她同样热烈的欢迎。莱斯特小姐的第一次公开演讲将于12月27日星期三晚上8时15分在公会堂教堂举行。

访问上海

英国著名社会工作者穆里尔·莱斯特（Muriel Lester）小姐将于下周访问上海。她作为“和解团契”（Fellowship of Reconciliation）的发起人之一而闻名，但更为人熟知的身份是伦敦东区金斯利大厅（Kingsley Hall）这一定居服务机构的创始人。

三十一年前，她萌生了服务的愿景，并将自己的生命奉献给伦敦贫民窟的穷人。她与姐姐创办了金斯利大厅，这是一个建立在自愿贫困基础上的基督教社会中心，她们将所有积蓄投入其中，并一直居住在那里。七年前，莱斯特小姐前往印度，与泰戈尔共度一个月，又与甘地共度一个月。两年前，甘地先生赴伦敦参加圆桌会议期间，在金斯利大厅与穷人们一起度过了整整三个月。金斯利大厅是一个位于大型工业区中心的团契中心，主要由当地居民自行运作。金斯利大厅没有受薪员工。这项东区社会工作拥有的支持者包括利顿勋爵（Lord Lytton）、西比尔·索恩代克夫人（Mrs. Sybil Thorndike）、约翰·梅斯菲尔德先生（Mr. John Masefield）、查尔斯·特里维廉爵士（Sir Charles Trevelyan）、阿斯特子爵夫人（Lady Astor）、克内布沃思子爵（Viscount Knebworth）、乔治·兰斯伯里先生（Mr. George Lansbury）等人士，以及许多其他像A. A. 米尔恩先生（Mr. A. A. Milne）那样通过捐赠屋顶花园来表达实际兴趣的人。这项工作如此成功，以至于人们要求并在达格纳姆（Dagenham）建立了第二座金斯利大厅，而专门用于儿童工作的建筑——“儿童之家”——目前也是该工作中一个活跃的单元。

莱斯特小姐夏季在美国演讲；在那里，一位作家称她为“英国的简·亚当斯”。11月下旬及12月期间，她在中国北部和中部地区演讲，目前身在南京。她在众多听众面前发表了充满激情的演讲，希望上海能在繁忙的节日季节给予她同样热烈的欢迎。莱斯特小姐的首次公开演讲将于12月27日（星期三）晚上8点15分在社区教堂（Community Church）举行。

（手写批注：Novel thing 《每日新闻》 1933年12月21日）

Confidential

Sir,

I have the honour to refer to your letter
of December 12, and to state that Miss Muriel Lester
is making a round the world tour by the N.Y.K. Line
in company with Mrs. Garry Hogg and Miss Rosemary Hogg.
The party arrived in Yokohama by the "Asama Maru" from
San Francisco on October 19, and efforts are at present
being made to trace their movements after that date.
So far as can be ascertained, Miss Lester and her
friends did not pass through Shanghai, and it is
believed that they journeyed from Japan to Hankow
also
via Tientsin or Tsingtao. It is believed that they
are suspected of being engaged in undesirable political
activities, as Mr. H.N. Steptoe requested the Special
Branch in the early part of this month to be on the
look out for Miss Lester's arrival.

According to information supplied by the
N.Y.K., Miss Lester is 49 years old. She is travelling
on British Passport No.4489 and gives her address in
the United Kingdom as "Kingsley Hall, Bow, London E.3".
Mrs. Garry Hogg is 32 years old and Miss Rosemary
Hogg is 21. They are both British subjects and give
their address in the United Kingdom as "Coverdale,
Grove Avenue, Mapperley, Nottingham".

REPORT
S.2, Special Branch.
Date December 14, 1933.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File Nos. B. REGI
No. D 5543
Date 14/12/33）

Subject (in full) Enquiry from H.B.M. Consulate-General regarding
Miss Muriel Lester.
Made W. and Forwarded by D.I. Everest

With reference to the attached letter dated December 12,
1933, from H.B.M. Consulate-General requesting information
regarding Miss Muriel Lester, I have to state that we have no
definite information regarding this lady's political activities
or of her having passed through Shanghai. It is believed,
however, that she is regarded with suspicion from a political
point of view by the British Home Authorities in so much that a request
to be on the look out for her arrival in Shanghai was received
verbally from Mr. H.N. Steptoe by the undersigned in the early
part of this month.

Discreet enquiries during the past two weeks disclosed
that a Miss Muriel Lester, British subject, age 49, holding
passport No. 4489, arrived in Yokohama in the N.Y.K. vessel
"Asama Maru" from San Francisco on October 19. She is on a
round the world tour and is accompanied by Mrs. Garry Hogg,
age 32, and Miss Rosemary Hogg, age 21, both British subjects.
Miss Lester's home address is given as "Kingsley Hall,
Bow, London, E.3," and that of Mrs. and Miss Hogg as "Coverdale
Grove Avenue, Mapperley, Nottingham."

Apart from the above we have no further information
regarding Miss Lester's movements. A watch has been kept
on all arrivals at this port and lists of incoming passengers
have been scrutinized. Enquiries at the local Chinese Passport
Examination Bureau have also been made with negative results.

It is possible that Miss Lester journeyed to Hankow from
Japan via Tientsin and Nanking and that she has not yet visited
Shanghai.

（批：JR）

D.I. Everest.
D. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

主题（完整）关于大不列颠陛下总领事馆就穆里尔·莱斯特小姐一事进行的查询。
由 W. 撰写并由警督埃弗勒斯转发

参照附件中日期为1933年12月12日的大不列颠陛下总领事馆来信，该信请求提供有关穆里尔·莱斯特小姐的信息，本人须声明，我们没有任何关于这位女士的政治活动或其曾途经上海的确切信息。然而，据信英国本土当局从政治角度对她持怀疑态度，因为本月早些时候，签署人收到了H.N. 斯蒂普托先生的口头请求，要求留意她抵达上海的情况。

过去两周内的谨慎调查显示，一位名为穆里尔·莱斯特的英国臣民，现年49岁，持有第4489号护照，于10月19日乘坐日本邮船会社的“浅间丸”号从旧金山抵达横滨。她正在进行环球旅行，随行人员有32岁的加里·霍格夫人和21岁的罗斯玛丽·霍格小姐，两人均为英国臣民。莱斯特小姐的家庭住址登记为“伦敦E.3区，鲍区，金斯利大厅”，霍格夫人和霍格小姐的地址登记为“诺丁汉，马普利，格罗夫大道，科夫代尔”。

除上述信息外，我们没有关于莱斯特小姐行踪的更多情报。已对本港所有抵达人员进行监视，并仔细审查了入境乘客名单。也向本地中国护照查验局进行了查询，但未获结果。

莱斯特小姐有可能从日本经天津和南京前往汉口，且尚未访问上海。

（批注：JR）

警督 埃弗勒斯。
